passage_text: Researchers conducted a randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a novel antihypertensive agent, Hypertenso, in adults with stage 1 hypertension. Participants (n = 200) were randomized to receive either Hypertenso (n = 100) or placebo (n = 100) for 12 weeks. Blood pressure was measured at baseline and at the end of the study. The investigators reported the mean systolic blood pressure (SBP) reduction and standard deviation (SD) for each group. The Hypertenso group experienced a mean SBP reduction of 12.4 mmHg (SD = 6.8), whereas the placebo group had a mean reduction of 3.1 mmHg (SD = 5.9). The authors concluded that Hypertenso significantly lowered SBP compared with placebo (p < 0.001) and suggested that the drug could be an effective treatment option for patients with stage 1 hypertension.
stem: What does the table most directly indicate about the effect of Hypertenso on systolic blood pressure?

options.A: Hypertenso reduced SBP by 9.3 mmHg more than placebo.
options.B: Hypertenso reduced SBP by 12.4 mmHg on average.
options.C: Placebo reduced SBP by 3.1 mmHg on average.
options.D: Both groups experienced the same magnitude of SBP reduction.

explanation: The mean reduction in the Hypertenso group (12.4 mmHg) exceeds that of the placebo group (3.1 mmHg) by 9.3 mmHg, indicating a greater effect of the drug.
trap: Option B focuses only on the Hypertenso group and ignores the comparative aspect with placebo.

stem: Which study design feature best supports the conclusion that Hypertenso caused the observed SBP reduction?

options.A: Randomization of participants to treatment groups.
options.B: Measurement of blood pressure at baseline and 12 weeks.
options.D: Reporting of mean SBP reduction and SD.

explanation: Randomization minimizes selection bias and balances known and unknown confounders, strengthening the causal inference that the drug caused the greater SBP reduction.
trap: Option B describes data collection timing, not the design element that ensures causality.

stem: What percent of the Hypertenso group’s mean SBP reduction is represented by the placebo group’s mean reduction?
explanation: Percent = (3.1/12.4) x 100 = 25.0%. The placebo reduction is exactly one quarter of the drug's.
trap: Option B (24.8%) is a small arithmetic slip; the ratio is exactly 0.25.

stem: Which statement is a misinterpretation of the SD (6.8 mmHg) reported for the Hypertenso group?

options.A: Roughly 68% of reductions fell between 5.6 and 19.2 mmHg, if reductions are approximately normal.
options.B: Every participant's reduction was exactly 6.8 mmHg away from the mean.
options.C: The SD is a measure of how spread out individual reductions are around the mean.
options.D: If reductions are roughly normal, about 95% fall between about -1.2 and 26.0 mmHg.

explanation: Correct: The SD is a typical (root-mean-square) deviation from the mean; individual participants deviate by varying amounts, not by exactly 6.8 mmHg. Why the others are wrong: A) mean plus or minus 1 SD (12.4 +/- 6.8 = 5.6 to 19.2) covers about 68% of values for roughly normal data. C) this is the correct definition of what an SD describes. D) mean plus or minus 2 SD (12.4 +/- 13.6) gives -1.2 to 26.0, covering about 95%.
trap: Treating the SD as the exact distance every participant lies from the mean, rather than a summary of typical spread.

stem: Which conclusion about Hypertenso is best supported by this trial?

options.A: Over 12 weeks in adults with stage 1 hypertension, Hypertenso lowered SBP about 9.3 mmHg more than placebo.
options.B: Hypertenso prevents strokes and heart attacks.
options.C: Hypertenso is superior to all other antihypertensive drugs.
options.D: The placebo group's 3.1 mmHg reduction shows Hypertenso had no effect beyond placebo.

explanation: Correct: Mean reductions were 12.4 mmHg versus 3.1 mmHg, a 9.3 mmHg greater reduction with Hypertenso after 12 weeks in stage 1 patients. Why the others are wrong: B) only SBP was measured, not cardiovascular events. C) no other drug was compared in the trial. D) the drug group's reduction was far larger than the placebo group's, so the drug had an effect beyond placebo.
trap: Extending a 12-week blood pressure result to cardiovascular outcomes or to head-to-head superiority that the trial never tested.
